input.question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?
input.ground_truth: Nothing. In 2015 alone, airplanes [carried ~3.441B people](_URL_0_). Most of them have devices with radios (phones, tablets, laptops). Many of them simply forgot to turn it off. There has never been a single malfunction of any sort attributed to a GSM/UMTS/LTE or WiFi radio not turned off. As a side note, FAA does not prohibit cellphone (much less WiFi) operation during flight, see 14 CFR 91.21 (b)(5); FCC and carriers do.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

I am a man.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Hypothetically what is the worst thing that could happen if I don't turn on "airplane mode"?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your phone is like a little radio. When you are on an airplane, the airplane needs to talk to the ground using big radios. If your phone is not in airplane mode, it might try to talk to cell towers (which are like phone towers on the ground) instead of listening to the airplane.

If your phone keeps talking to the cell towers while you're flying high up, it could get confused and mess things up a little bit. It might use up your phone’s battery really fast, or it could try to connect to lots of towers very quickly, which is not good for the airplane’s radios.

But the *worst* thing that could happen is that it might cause a tiny problem with the airplane’s radios, but actually, airplanes are made to be safe even if phones are on. Still, it’s better to use airplane mode so your phone doesn’t waste battery and doesn’t try to talk to the ground when it should be quiet.
